description: A four-panel composite of three-dimensional bar charts, all in the same grey-wall rendering style, reporting the machine-learning workflow that links FeMnAlC steel composition to microstructure. (a) plots "Cross validation accuracy" (y axis, labelled 0.0 to 1.0 in steps of 0.2) against five "Algorithms" (x axis: KNN, ANN, SVM, RF, CART), with legend entries Y3 (orange), Y2 (green) and Y1 (purple); every bar of KNN, SVM, RF and CART reaches the 1.0 gridline, whereas ANN's Y3 bar falls to about the 0.65 level, between the 0.6 and 0.8 gridlines, and its Y1 bar sits just below 1.0. The remaining panels each plot "Mean Decrease Accuracy(%)" against eight "Removed descriptor" categories, always ordered Mn, Al, C, Fe, VEC, Tm, ΔSmix, ΔHmix and joined by a grey line: (b) "A single γ region (Y3)", y axis 0-40; (c) "A γ+κ dual-phase region at 500–600 °C (Y2)", y axis 0-16; (d) "The existence of the κ phase (Y1)", y axis 0-50. Al gives the tallest bar in (b) and (d); Mn and Fe give the tallest bars in (c), where C is the shortest bar. The group argues that RF is the best classifier and that Al, then Mn and Fe, dominate descriptor importance.

subfigures.description: 3D grouped bar chart; y axis 'Cross validation accuracy' from 0.0 to 1.0 (ticks every 0.2), x axis 'Algorithms' with KNN, ANN, SVM, RF, CART; legend Y3 (orange), Y2 (green), Y1 (purple). All bars reach the 1.0 gridline except for ANN, whose Y3 bar is roughly at the 0.65 level and whose Y1 bar is slightly below 1.0.

3D bar chart titled 'A single γ region (Y3)'. Y axis 'Mean Decrease Accuracy(%)' from 0 to 40 (ticks every 5); x axis 'Removed descriptor' with Mn, Al, C, Fe, VEC, Tm, ΔSmix, ΔHmix. Al produces the tallest bar (above the 40 % gridline), VEC and Tm are next, and C is the shortest bar (near the 12-13 % level).

3D bar chart titled 'A γ+κ dual-phase region at 500–600 °C (Y2)'. Y axis 'Mean Decrease Accuracy(%)' from 0 to 16 (ticks every 2); same eight descriptors on the x axis. Mn and Fe are the two tallest bars (reaching roughly the 15 and 15 % gridlines), VEC and Tm follow around 13.5 and 11.5 %, and C is the shortest bar at about the 6.5 % level.

3D bar chart titled 'The existence of the κ phase (Y1)', printed in the image with the corner label '(a)' even though the caption assigns it as panel (d). Y axis 'Mean Decrease Accuracy(%)' from 0 to 50 (ticks every 10); same eight descriptors. Al is by far the tallest bar (about the 50-52 % level), VEC is second (about 27 %), ΔHmix and Mn follow, and C is the shortest bar (just below 10 %).

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a grouped 3D bar chart whose legend has three entries, Y3 (orange), Y2 (green) and Y1 (purple), one per classification target.

In panel (a) the bars for KNN, SVM, RF and CART all reach the 1.0 gridline of the 'Cross validation accuracy' axis for Y1, Y2 and Y3, while ANN's Y3 bar is by far the lowest, lying between the 0.6 and 0.8 gridlines.
The x axis of panels (b), (c) and (d) is labelled 'Removed descriptor' and lists the same eight categories in identical order: Mn, Al, C, Fe, VEC, Tm, ΔSmix, ΔHmix.
The y axis of panels (b), (c) and (d) is 'Mean Decrease Accuracy(%)', scaled 0–40 (ticks every 5) in (b), 0–16 (ticks every 2) in (c), and 0–50 (ticks every 10) in (d).
In panel (b), titled 'A single γ region (Y3)', the Al bar is the tallest and rises above the 40 % gridline, whereas the C bar is the shortest, at roughly the 12–13 % level.
In panel (c), titled 'A γ+κ dual-phase region at 500–600 °C (Y2)', the Mn and Fe bars are the two tallest (both around the 15 % gridline), and the C bar is the shortest, around the 6.5 % level.
In panel (d), titled 'The existence of the κ phase (Y1)', the Al bar is by far the tallest (about the 50 % gridline) and the C bar is the shortest (just below the 10 % gridline).

The fourth panel is printed with the corner label '(a)' although its in-panel title is 'The existence of the κ phase (Y1)'; the caption assigns this content to panel (d), so the printed panel letter conflicts with the caption numbering.

The caption states that panel (a) compares different machine learning methods, (b) gives the relative importance of 8 descriptors for a single γ region, (c) for a (γ+κ) region in 500–600 °C, and (d) for the existence of the κ-phase.
The citing text states that five algorithms (KNN, ANN, SVM, RF and CART) were trained with 10-fold cross-validation, and that all but ANN performed well with CVA values from above 0.9 to less than 1.
The citing text reports that RF achieved the best performance, with CVA values of 0.98 (Y1), 0.98 (Y2) and 0.96 (Y3), and that RF was therefore chosen as the most appropriate algorithm.

The citing text asserts that Al plays the most significant role in the partial classification problems (a single γ region and κ exists), because accuracy decreased the most when Al was removed from the descriptor set.
The citing text asserts that Mn and Fe are the most important descriptors for the (γ+κ) region in 500–600 °C classification (Fig. 3c) and that C has the least effect on the model.

The citing text asserts that C had no significant impact on the presence of the κ phase, whose precipitation is primarily governed by Al, and that the descriptor ranking was input into the model in descending order of mean decrease accuracy.
